ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state structure with several curved arrows; the problem requires ignoring these arrows. The main body is two fused six-membered carbon rings on the left and right, sharing a middle C-C bond. The upper bridgehead position is connected to an oxygen atom marked with a negative charge. From the ring below extends a nitrogen-containing substituent, in which C-N, N=N, and N-S can be seen in order, and S is an SO2Ar fragment, that is, sulfur is connected to two oxygens and one Ar aryl group. Reasoning and counting: Ignore all hydrogen-related bonds and curved arrows, and count only independent bond connections between non-hydrogen atoms. If the two fused six-membered carbon rings are counted separately as 6 edges and 6 edges, the central shared C-C bond can be counted only once, so the number of carbon-skeleton C-C bonds is 6 + 6 - 1 = 11. Add 1 more upper bridgehead C-O bond. The lower substituent bonds are: ring C-N 1, N=N 1, N-S 1, two S=O bonds 2, S-Ar 1, totaling 6. Ar as a visible abbreviation needs to be expanded as an aromatic ring, and there are 6 aromatic C-C bonds inside the aromatic ring. The total is 11 + 1 + 6 + 6 = 24.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows. Count unique non-hydrogen bond connections by tracing the image. Around the fused bicyclic carbon framework, count the left six-membered ring and the right six-membered ring, counting their shared central bond only once: this gives 11 C-C bonds. Add the single C-O bond to the oxygen above the bridgehead. Add the substituent bonds below: ring C-N, N=N, N-S, two S=O bonds, and S-Ar, giving 6 more. Finally expand the visible shorthand Ar as an aryl ring and add its 6 internal aromatic C-C bonds. Sum 11 + 1 + 6 + 6 = 24.
